correctness.rationale: For any finite permutation π on n>=1, P its integer permutation matrix, |a| coordinate sum, K=ker |.|, and A=I-P, the twisted sum a⋆b=a+P^{|a|}b is associative with inverse -P^{-|a|}a and the nonnegative monoid generates its fraction group. Commutator (a⋆b)(b⋆a)^(-1)=(I-P^t)a-(I-P^s)b lies in AK; the basis generator commutators A(e_i-e_j) show γ2=AK. Conjugating degree-zero vectors by any degree-one element acts as P, so γ_r=A^{r-1}K for every r>=2. On a cycle with a mixed-prime divisor d, integral W_d=ker Φ_d(P) is nonzero and A acts as a lattice automorphism since Φ_d(1)=1, yielding a nonzero element in every γ_r. Conversely for prime-power cycles every nonzero eigenvalue 1-ζ of A on the root lattice L=im(A) is a nonunit (Φ_{p^j}(1)=p). A nonzero stabilized integral intersection J=∩A^jL would force an integer-lattice automorphism with only nonunit eigenvalues, contradiction; J=0 and residual nilpotence follows. This holds for mixed disjoint prime-power cycles of different primes (order need not be prime-power), and nonidentity π is never actually nilpotent.
